title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-oliver-kim
content:
PR: #8273 — kv-cache batching refactor (WIP)
Owner: @morgan (TBD)
Goal: Reduce token generation tail latency for small requests while keeping high throughput for long sequences.

Quick summary notes:
- Main change: split KV cache into per-shard LRU + global lookup table to reduce O(N) scan when inserting cache entries.
- Introduces BatchBuilder abstraction to handle mixed-length batching with sticky routing to avoid re-sharding hot KV keys.
- Added optional adaptive_batch_timeout config (ms) to trade latency for throughput.

Top-level review checklist:
- [ ] Correctness: unit tests cover edge cases (empty KV, duplicate keys, eviction ordering)
- [ ] Performance: microbench for 1-64 seq len with and without sticky routing
- [ ] Safety: ensure no race between cache eviction and KV reads (concurrency model)
- [ ] Backwards compat: config defaults should preserve previous behavior (adaptive timeout = 0)
- [ ] CI flakiness: stress tests on CI for 30s with parallel requests to catch races

Notes from running local perf tests (10/28):
- baseline (master) median p95 for 16-token avg: 42ms; branch: 48ms when adaptive timeout disabled (regression)
- enabling sticky routing improves p95 to 35ms but reduces throughput by ~6% for long sequences (>=512)
- observed small memory regression (~3%) due to per-shard index overhead; need to quantify for target GPU sizes

Code-level observations / suggestions:
- batch_builder.go line 128: explicit copy of requests slice — consider using slice header re-slice to avoid allocation in hot path
- kv_cache.go: eviction callback runs synchronously; should it be async to avoid blocking insert? add metrics if change introduced
- concurrency: use of sync.RWMutex around global map looks fine, but nested locking when shard lock acquired can deadlock if order not preserved — add comment and test that enforces lock ordering
- tests/kv_cache_test.go: add property test for random ops sequence + reference implementation to assert invariants (size, eviction order)

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- (blocker?) Re-evaluate default adaptive_batch_timeout: current heuristic (mean + 2*std) causes added latency for many 8-64 token workloads; propose default 0 and opt-in via config for now
- Add telemetry: per-route cache hit rate + eviction rate + per-shard size distribution exposed to console
- Add documentation snippet for migration: known perf tradeoffs, knobs to tune (sticky routing, shard count, adaptive timeout)
- Write a canary plan: roll to 5% traffic dedicated pool for 24h, monitor p95 and throughput, abort thresholds set at +20% p95 or -10% throughput

Questions for author:
- Is memory overhead per model tagged anywhere? If not, we should add a metric to attribute cache memory to model/version to avoid surprises in multi-tenant Dedicated pools.
- Are there any compatibility requirements with older runtime clients? I saw a TODO about serialization format change in kv_cache.proto — needs sign-off.

Patch-specific nitpicks:
- Small style: prefer early-return pattern in batch_builder.go reduce indentation
- Log messages: swap some Debugf -> Tracef for high-frequency paths (instrumentation team prefers Trace to avoid logs noise)

Quick prioritization (for author):
1) Add tests for concurrency and eviction ordering (high)
2) Add perf microbench for typical PLG workloads (16-64 tokens) (high)
3) Add telemetry hooks (medium)
4) Rework eviction callback to be async/metrics safe (medium)
5) Document config defaults and migration note (low)

Slack/PR comments I plan to leave:
- "Thanks! overall design looks promising. Left some nit comments and a couple of concurrency tests I'd like to see before approving. Can we also get a small perf run across 1/16/64/512 token workloads?"
- "Re: adaptive_batch_timeout — let's default it off for now and iterate; add a follow-up ticket to explore heuristics with live traffic."

Related tickets / refs:
- JIRA-4721: kv-cache eviction bug (long-standing)
- PR 8012: initial batching prototype (historical, useful for tests)
- confluence: serving-runtime/kv-cache-optimization (design notes)

Personal TODOs (quick):
- run full CI + stress on my dev rig and paste numbers here (10/30)
- prototype async eviction callback (branch: oliver/async-evict)
summary: scratchpad for code review of PR #8273 (kv-cache batching refactor)
